hypothesis: Shorting Binance USDT perps on cliff unlocks of at least 10% of unlocked supply (t-7 to t-1) and on Upbit KRW listings (D0 to D0+7), with fills taken from real books before the daily close and an equal-notional long in the 30 most-traded perps, earns a positive hedged return after funding and costs, and it does not rest on the fill being the daily close.

events.sources: read-only: data/research/unlock_short_t7/tracker.json and data/research/upbit_krw_listing/tracker.json. They supply the event, its symbol and when it became known, and nothing else. No price, return or status of theirs enters a result.
events.unlock: stream U: a source trade with a symbol and size_pct >= 10. Short at the entry window of the source's entry_day (t-7), cover at the window of its exit_day (t-1).
events.krw_listing: stream K: a source trade with a symbol, not backfilled, status not no_perp or delisted. The source's universe stands: a perp listed before the notice and a Binance spot daily bar exactly 30 days before it. One listing per coin per 30 days, also the source's. Short at the window of the notice's UTC day (D0), cover at the window of D0+7.
events.left_out: Upbit caution notices and 5-10% unlocks are not in this ledger: neither beat the same coin's other windows in the holdout (see development_evidence). Adding either needs a new protocol.
events.first_seen: an event is journaled at the first pass that sees it, with its size frozen. Only events whose entry window closes after activation are recorded. An event the source marks late, or first seen after its entry window opens, is void with reason late and stays in the revision count.

execution.window: 23:55:00 to 23:59:30 UTC. The web job passes every 20 seconds inside it. It is before the close on purpose: Upbit-listed coins fell 2.17% on average in the first hour after the D0 close (54 holdout events, t = -3.75), and books the trackers read 3 to 28 minutes after that close already stood 2.58% lower on average.
execution.coin_leg: short at the best bid on entry, cover at the best ask on exit, both from a fresh 100-level book. The walked price for the declared order is recorded as well, to check the impact model.
execution.basket_leg: long, equal notional across 30 perps, frozen at entry: USDT perpetuals with contract type PERPETUAL, status TRADING, underlying type COIN, base asset neither a stablecoin nor a gold token, ranked by rolling 24-hour quote volume at the capture, the coin itself left out. Bought at the best ask and sold at the best bid from one bookTicker read. Not inherited from the source's basket, which has 119-123 coins.
execution.exit: time exit at the window of the exit day. A stop or a revision closes at the first window at or after it was seen. A coin no longer trading exits at its last hourly close, reason delisted. A window missed for any reason is captured at the next pass, and the delay is recorded.
execution.stop: +40% on hourly highs from the entry close, checked every pass and just before an exit capture; a time exit waits for a readable check until its window ends. Fill 2% beyond the level, or beyond the bar's open if it gapped through; time = the end of that bar. The basket stays until the next window, as in the backtest.
execution.same_coin: a coin already held voids a later event with reason coin_already_held. Exits are captured before entries inside a window, so a coin leaving today can be shorted again today. Same day: unlock first, then listing.
execution.funding: real settlements, each rate x settlement mark / own entry price, in (entry, exit]. The position opens before the settlement at the entry close, so that one counts, and closes before the one at the exit close, so that one does not; both legs alike. Read in the latest-N form only. A history that cannot reach the entry, or a gap longer than 8 hours, is retried and never booked as zero. After 7 days a gap is recorded on the outcome, basket members with no history are dropped and listed (at least 20 must remain), and a trade whose coin funding still cannot be read is void as unresolved.
execution.costs: coin 0.20% and basket 0.10% round trip, as in the backtest, plus square-root impact on both legs and both sides: sigma x sqrt(order / rolling 24-hour quote volume), for an order of 10,000 USDT per leg (a 200,000 account at 5% per trade) and order/30 per basket member. Sigma is the sample deviation of the last 30 daily returns, 0.10 when there are fewer than 10. Impact is a model and is not calibrated to fills; the median walked-book slippage is reported next to it.
execution.cap: a second figure limits each basket member's price gain to +100%, since one member's +958% made +56.7% of the best trade in the history. The uncapped figure is what the position would have earned; the capped one is what does not depend on such luck. Both must clear the review.

schedule_revisions.record: one local snapshot per UTC day, from the tracker's schedule cache: index hash; for every cached token its cliffs of at least 5% from t-7 to t+120 and, where it has any, the file hash. Stored gzipped under schedule_snapshots/, hash journaled. This starts the point-in-time evidence the backtest lacks.
schedule_revisions.revised: an unlock with no cliff of at least 7.5% within 3 days of its frozen date in today's snapshot. A token with no schedule file proves nothing. Before entry: void with reason revised_before_entry. After entry: exit at the next window, reason revised, return still counted and reported on the trade.

analysis.unit: batch = the entered trades sharing an entry day, both streams; batch return = their mean hedged return; a batch counts once every trade in it has an outcome
analysis.primary: mean hedged return of the batches
analysis.review: one review, journaled once and then frozen: at the first pass where the first 30 entry days are all complete, or 365 days after activation, whichever first. By count it uses those 30 entry days; by time it uses all complete batches. Before the review the summary is descriptive and computes no p-value.
analysis.test: one-sided sign-flip of the batch returns, statistic the mean, 10,000 draws, numpy default_rng with the seed in parameters

verdict.insufficient: fewer than 15 complete batches at the review
verdict.rejected: batch mean <= +2.0%, or capped batch mean <= +2.0%
verdict.partly_rejected: otherwise, if a stream or the entry rule is rejected below
verdict.inconclusive: otherwise, if p > 0.05 or the two-best-coins test fails
verdict.supported_uptrend_uncovered: otherwise, when fewer than 10 unlock trades entered after a rise

stream_tests.mean: stream U or K with at least 15 trades and mean <= +1.0%: that stream is rejected. A stream with fewer trades is reported as too_few and cannot be rejected on its mean.
stream_tests.schedule: with at least 10 unlock events, more than 15% of them revised, moved, removed or late: U is rejected. The backtest assumes zero.
stream_tests.uptrend: at least 10 unlock trades entered with the prior 60-day move of a daily-rebalanced top-30 index above +15%: if their mean <= 0, U is rejected. With fewer than 10 the result says the rise was not covered. In the reference this group earned +0.58% over 23 trades, against +4.51% and +8.95% in the other two.
stream_tests.entry_rule: the first 15 K trades, or all of them when at least 8 at the review: mean gap between the entry price and that day's close <= -1.0 points rejects the entry rule, since this ledger then does not get the close's price either
stream_tests.two_best_coins: the mean hedged return of the trades outside the 2 coins with the largest total must exceed +2.0%

analysis.expected_power: drawing 30 reference batches without replacement, shifted to a target mean, with the mean, capped-mean, significance and two-best-coins tests (the batch t-statistic stands in for the sign-flip test; the other stream tests cannot be run on history). All history: at the reference mean of +6.30% 74.6% pass, 5.1% rejected; at half 25.5% pass, 41.4% rejected; at zero 1.7% pass, 90.1% rejected. Since 2025: 80.2% / 2.8%; 23.3% / 42.3%; 1.0% / 93.7%. A pass here does not cover the rising-market condition, which 30 batches will probably not reach: about 18% of reference unlocks qualify, so about 4 trades.
analysis.pace: 4.15 reference batches a month over all history and 5.84 since 2025, so 30 batches would take about 5 to 7 months
analysis.alerts: drawdown of -8% on settled trades (5% per trade, in exit order, open positions not marked; the reference's worst is -3.12%), or one hedged trade at -70% or worse (the reference's worst is -55.27%), journal a safety alert once and show on the tracker page. The ledger keeps recording: on paper, stopping would only lose the sample.
analysis.reported: per-stream trades, means, stops and revisions; capped mean; costs and funding by leg; entry gap to the close; spread, depth at 1%, walked-book slippage against modelled impact; void counts by reason; the coin's return from mid prices
analysis.first_hour_evidence: one-minute bars from 30 minutes before the entry close to 2 hours after it are saved per trade, because the cause of the first-hour fall is unknown and local history is hourly. This is not used in any verdict.
analysis.no_tuning: no change of thresholds, unit, review or tests after activation; a change needs a new protocol id and directory

development_evidence.reference_file: data/research/event_short_preclose_v1/development_reference.csv, from scripts/event_short_preclose_reference.py on local data through 2026-11-03
development_evidence.archive_file: data/research/event_short_preclose_v1/development_archive.tar.gz: the account study's protocol, code and results, the red team's report and code, and the author's re-check
development_evidence.reference_rule: this ledger's universe, stop, funding boundary, fixed costs and impact, except that the daily close stands in for the 23:55 fill and the spread is not charged. Entries from 2022-11. Schedules: the tracker's cache, then the study's for tokens that have left it.
development_evidence.same_coin_other_windows_holdout: same coin within 60 days of age, hedged, same costs, author's re-check (coin clustered p): >=10% unlock +7.19 vs +0.27 (0.003); KRW +6.06 vs +0.57 (0.003); 5-10% unlock +1.50 vs +0.83 (0.31); caution +1.46 vs -0.09 (0.32)
development_evidence.krw_against_similar_pumps_holdout: 53 events +5.61 against coins with a similar day's rise and volume surge -2.69, difference +8.30 (p 0.0002); dev +9.32 (p 0.02)
development_evidence.stress: from the account study on a slightly different universe (Sharpe 3.63 at the start): removing one token outside the study's universe, capping members, consistent funding and $200k impact 2.88; entering 1 hour after the close as well 2.05, 4 hours after 1.78. This ledger's rule is the 2.88 line, with the fill before the close.
development_evidence.status: in sample. The event edges were found on this data; the >=10% split and dropping caution were chosen after seeing it; the holdout was only new for the account construction, and yearly holdout figures were seen in a dry run before it was formally opened. The holdout was also a falling alt market (top-30 index -72% in 2025, -68% in 2026 to November). This ledger is the first independent test, and the reference is not the expected result.
development_evidence.already_seen_and_excluded: events entered before activation are development data: forward-era reference trades NMR, KAIA, NOM, GTC, RSR, APR, BMT, NIL

red_team_changes: The red team's draft review rules (redteam/REPORT.md in the archive) were kept except: the top-2-coins share above 50% became the mean without the 2 best coins, because the share rule blocked 13.7% of draws at the reference mean while the new one blocks 4.0% and halves false passes; the entry-gap test also accepts 8 to 14 K trades at the review, because 30 batches hold about 13; the drawdown and single-trade lines warn and do not stop a paper ledger; the stop-fill line is dropped, because the backtest barely moves with worse stop fills (Sharpe 3.54 at 5% worse, 3.39 at 10%) and one-minute evidence is saved anyway.
limits: The history covers tokens still listed by DefiLlama and Binance when it was collected, and schedules as known in 2026. The forward record is what starts to answer whether schedules were known at t-7; its first 38 days showed no change to any >=10% cliff, which cannot exclude meaningful revision over two years.

Paper fills at the best quote plus a model. It places no order, so it cannot see queue, rejected orders, position limits, reduce-only states, margin or auto-deleveraging. 31 orders per trade are assumed to fill within seconds.
A 23:55 fill is not a daily close: entry gap and exit gap are measured, and the reference's returns may not carry over. A market order just before 00:00 UTC meets whatever liquidity that moment has.
The web job must be up inside the window. A missed entry is void and counted. Outages are unrelated to returns, but many of them would thin the sample.
Tokens repeat and batches overlap. Returns are skewed to the right: in the reference the best 20 of 127 trades made 70% of the total.

The rising-market condition will probably stay uncovered at the review, and the data has no reliable sample of a 2021-style alt rally: 2021 has 8 listings (+9.13%) and 10 unlocks (+4.23%), survivors only, and 2020-2022 unlocks together earned -0.57% over 17 trades.

integrity.journal: data/research/event_short_preclose_v1/journal.jsonl, append-only and hash-chained; each record carries the SHA-256 of this file and core/research/event_short_preclose_ledger.py; any change stops the journal
integrity.paper_only: records only; never places or proposes orders
